item.title: Composite witness sieves, Kneser--Plancherel containers, and the exponent $5/7$ for the Erd\H{o}s--Straus conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.08717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation $4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$, Vaughan's unconditional bound on the exceptional set $E(N)$ has stood at $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c(\log N)^{2/3})$ since 1970. We harness composite divisor witnesses at growing depth to cross this $2/3$ barrier unconditionally. On the full exceptional set $E(N)$, we prove the unconditional bound $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c'(\log N)^{5/7}/(\log\log N)^{2/7})$, improving the exponent to $5/7$ (with an intermediate stage at $7/10$). On the structured component $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))$, an algebraic and spectral container hierarchy combined with a generating-polynomial large sieve reaches the exponent $1-o(1)$: $|E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))|\ll_\kappa N\exp(-(\frac{1}{40960}+o(1))\frac{\log N}{(\log\log N)(\log\log\log N)^{\kappa}})$, matching the CRT capacity scale. These results resolve the obstructions to composite-witness sieving at growing depth. First, we replace subgroup generation by Kneser's stabilizer $K(M)$, which embeds into a $2$-primary character kernel, reducing container counts from $2^{\Theta(J^{4})}$ to $\exp(\mathcal{O}(J^{2}\log\log J))$. Coupling this with a generating-polynomial large sieve, Markov $1/2$-popular symmetry containers, and Pontryagin--Plancherel character containers yields the exponent $1-o(1)$ on $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}$. Second, to bypass unlocalized diffuse divisor sheets without subset enumeration, we construct a semi-composite congruence sieve $s=pq\equiv-1\pmod{12ua}$ ($p\in(Z^{9/10},Z]$, $q\le Q$ rough). Conditioning on $n\bmod M_{\mathrm{small}}$ yields CRT mutual independence while decoupling the modulus $12ua\le 12Z^{1/4}$ from $q$; a Bonferroni majorant and the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem then yield the unconditional $5/7$ exponent on all of $E(N)$. Finally, we study bilinear dispersion on $4uavw-4u^{2}v-w=n$ and difference sets $D(K_c)$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Dahan

item.title: Burgess' bounds with prime moduli
item.description: arXiv:2611.08816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_{\chi}(N)= \sum_{n\leq N} \chi(n)$, where $\chi$ is a Dirichlet character modulo a prime $p$. For integral $r\geq 2$, Burgess gave bounds of the shape $S_{\chi}(N) \ll N^{1-1/r} p^{(r+1)/(4r^{2})} \log p$. The factor of $\log p$ was reduced by several authors. We show that it can be removed completely.
item.dc:creator: Bryce Kerr, James Punch, Tim Trudgian

item.title: Joint Approximation and the Mixed-Prime Character Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.08964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the integer metric defined by the square denominators of two distinct primes, we prove simultaneous approximation to zero in one prime metric and to any prescribed integer in the other. A normalized convolution argument gives a uniform central spectral bound. Random relative translations of smooth weights produce an exact positive cas cade; Fourier positivity places every normalized finer convolution below its value at zero. A far-field recursion, the growth of merged square powers, and a two-term logarithmic-form estimate give summable fac tor bounds. Consequently, for every fixed pair of distinct primes p,q, the mixed continuous character group is Z[1/(pq)]/Z: no irrational pa rameter is continuous. The mixed completion is the product of the one-prime completions. For each fixed pair this also gives a compati ble rational join and a strictly finer compatible join of the associated real TVG topologies, with the same prescribed real character group. Exact witness search terminates at every strict precision and integer target. We retain the structural, density, divisibility, sequence and finite-certificate results leading to this proof. The existence argument does not give practical witness-size or runtime bounds, and it does not assume independence or equidistribution of the two digit systems. Se lected abstract components have been checked using Lean and Mathlib; the complete analytic argument has not been formalized. The corre sponding problem for three or more primes remains separate.
item.dc:creator: Irina Yaroshevskaya

item.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].
item.dc:creator: Khaled Qazaqzeh, Aymen Rawashdeh

item.title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields, II
item.description: arXiv:2611.09031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every number field of odd degree $n\geq 3$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has an integral defining polynomial whose coefficients are $O_n(D^{(n-1)/(2n-1)})$ in size. This strengthens, in odd-degree cases, the recently established bound of $O_n(D^{1/2})$ for all degrees $n$, which was conjectured in 1998 by Ruppert and is now known to be optimal in even degrees. More generally, we prove that this strengthened bound holds for all degree-$n$ fields having a real embedding and no subfield of index two. The proof makes use of the lattice shapes of the ring of integers and its trace dual, the inverse different. Assuming the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, as recently announced by Cureton and Thorner, we obtain an exponent smaller than $1/2$ for every field with no index-two subfield, of any signature. In the case of primitive fields, we obtain the exponent $(n-1)/(2n)$. In particular, we prove that the optimal exponent for cubic fields is $1/3$.
item.dc:creator: Manjul Bhargava, Sameera Vemulapalli

item.title: Campana points on quadrics with hyperplane boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.09148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Q\subset\mathbf P^{d+1}_k$ be a smooth quadric of dimension $d\ge2$ over a number field, and let $H_i=Q\cap\Pi_i$ be hyperplane sections for $1\le i\le d$. For every integer $m\ge2$, we prove Campana strong approximation for the pair $\bigl(Q,(1-1/m)(H_1+\cdots+H_d)_{\mathrm{red}}\bigr)$.
item.dc:creator: Dasheng Wei

item.title: Elliptic units, derived Heegner classes and the p-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer quotient of CM elliptic curves of rank two
item.description: arXiv:2611.09192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E\colon y^2=x^3-Dx$ have rank two and let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be a prime of good reduction. We study the conjecture that the $p$-adic quotient $q_p$, the leading coefficient of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function divided by the Euler factor and the $p$-adic regulator, equals the complex quotient $q_\infty=L''(E,1)/(2\Omega_E\mathrm{Reg}_\infty)$, and that the latter is rational. In rank one the analogous statement is a theorem of Perrin-Riou and Rubin, because a Heegner point computes both sides; in rank two there is no such point. We show that $q_p$ is the constant of the quadratic term of the two-variable Katz measure; this is how the conjecture arises, and it computes $q_p$ modulo any power of $p$ from critical Hecke $L$-values. We then show that $q_p$ is the coordinate of two global classes: Rubin's rank-two elliptic-unit class, whose position in $E(\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{Q}_p$ is $q_p$ times an explicit vector, and the derived Heegner class over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field $F$, for which we prove an exact identity. As consequences, whenever such a field $F$ satisfying our hypotheses exists, $q_p$ is a square in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ times the product of the Tamagawa numbers of $E$, so that the unit $q_p/A_E$ of the $p$-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula is a square when Sha is finite; if moreover the derived Heegner class has non-zero formal logarithm, the conjecture of Agboola and Castella for $E/F$ holds up to a $p$-adic unit, and with a theorem of Burungale, Castella and Skinner the anticyclotomic main conjecture holds integrally; and our conjecture is equivalent to the analytic form of theirs, with the products of anticyclotomic heights read sesquilinearly, which differs by a sign from its literal formulation. The conjecture is verified modulo $p^3$ for 5520 pairs $(E,p)$ with conductors up to $3.9\cdot10^{12}$, including curves with analytic Sha of order 4 and 9.
item.dc:creator: Miquel Calonge Fabregat

item.title: Bounded Ratios of Best Approximations: Sharp Bounds and Spectra of Diophantine Exponents
item.description: arXiv:2611.09206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve Problems 1, 2, and 3 posed by Marnat, Moshchevitin, and Schleischitz (arXiv:2505.15964). We consider totally irrational real n-by-m matrices and two conditions on their sequences of best approximations: (B) bounded successive height ratios and (C) bounded successive error ratios. Under (C), we prove that the ordinary Diophantine exponent is at most m and, when both dimensions are at least two, that the uniform exponent is at most m^2/(m+1). Combining these bounds with known results, we determine the individual spectra of both exponents under (C), with and without the additional assumption (B). When both dimensions are at least two, imposing (B) changes neither spectrum. A key ingredient is a block lemma for consecutive best approximations lying in a fixed rational subspace.
item.dc:creator: Maksim Lavrov

item.title: Root sharing and $2$-adic interpolation for Legendre polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.09312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach \`a la Skolem, that for a root $\alpha\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(\alpha)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.
item.dc:creator: Borys Kadets, Dan Mangoubi

item.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers among polynomial values
item.description: arXiv:2611.09386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\phi$ be a fixed polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and degree $k\geq2$. We prove that the values $2\phi(n)$, $1\leq n\leq N$, can be written as the sum of two primes, apart from at most $N^{\alpha_k+o(1)}$ exceptional indices, where $\alpha_k<1$. For quadratic polynomials the exponent is $1/2$, for cubic polynomials $5/8$, for quartic polynomials $3/4$, and for $k>4$ it is $1-1/(k+1)$. The proof combines a fourth-moment estimate over primes with mean-value estimates over arbitrary subsets of polynomial sequences.
item.dc:creator: I. Alth\"ofer, D. Chen, A. Perelli, J. Pintz

item.title: Curves with absolutely irreducible Tate modules over $p$-adic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.09393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over every number field, curves whose Jacobians have absolutely irreducible $\ell$-adic Tate modules exist in every positive genus and can be chosen hyperelliptic. Over $p$-adic fields, however, inertia and Frobenius can exclude entire genera. We classify the genera that occur for $\ell\ne p$ in terms of the residue characteristic and the cardinality of the residue field. For odd $p$, we also classify the genera occurring for hyperelliptic curves. These genera have relative density zero among those occurring for arbitrary curves, yielding Jacobians whose isogeny classes contain no hyperelliptic Jacobian. For odd $p$ and even residue degree, we obtain further restrictions on the genus when the curve itself is required to have potentially good reduction. Over number fields, we obtain uniform bounds from absolute irreducibility of the Tate module at two finite places of distinct residue characteristics different from $\ell$. The dimension of the abelian variety alone bounds the number of isomorphism classes in its isogeny class and the least degrees of isogenies between them.
item.dc:creator: Alexandros Konstantinou

item.title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.09629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. For an odd prime power $q$, consider polynomials over $\mathbb F_{q^n}$ of the form $\sum_{0\le i\le j<n}a_{ij}x^{q^i+q^j}+L(x)$, where $a_{ij}\in\mathbb F_{q^n}$ and $L$ serves as an $\mathbb F_q$-linear endomorphism of $\mathbb F_{q^n}$. In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not $2$, and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Ruikai Chen

item.title: On a Problem of Gordon and Hughes: The 11-adic Properties of Meromorphic Modular Functions on $\mathrm{X}_0(22)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Congruence families occur throughout the theory of modular forms. These families superficially resemble one another, though they can vary substantially in their overall difficulty. One major complication resides in the topology of the modular curve associated with a given congruence family. All previously studied families are associated with curves of genus 0 or 1. The existence of a family associated with a curve of genus 2 (and the associated difficulties of a proof thereof) was first speculated upon by Gordon and Hughes. We give the first explicit congruence family associated with $\mathrm{X}_0(22)$, a modular curve of genus 2, and prove it. We also propose two families of conjectures associated with the same modular curve.
item.dc:creator: Koustav Banerjee, Nicolas Allen Smoot

item.title: Euler trace congruences over local fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.09711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\QQ_p$ with uniformizer $\pi$ and residue field $\FF_q$. For each $r\ge1$, we determine the largest integer $E_r$ such that $\Tr(A^{q^r})\equiv\Tr(A^{q^{r-1}})\pmod{\pi^{E_r}}$ for every integral matrix $A$ with a prescribed residual similarity class. We give formulas for both nilpotent and nonnilpotent residual classes and construct integral lifts attaining the resulting exponents. We also exhibit local fields with the same ramification index and residue field for which the optimal exponents differ, even when $r$ and the residual similarity class are fixed.
item.dc:creator: Tao Wei, Xuejun Guo

item.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.09753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
item.dc:creator: William Verreault, Max Wenqiang Xu

item.title: Mellin Transform formulas for special values of Goss $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present paper, we provide formulas for the special values of dual Goss $L$-functions of Drinfeld modules at any non-negative integer in terms of the determinant of the values of a motivic map, extensively studied by both authors in 2026, for a large class of Anderson modules. Our result may be seen as a function field analogue of conjectural formulas for special values of motivic $L$-functions in terms of algebraic Mellin integrals.
item.dc:creator: O\u{g}uz Gezmi\c{s}, Nathan Green

item.title: Counting Finite Maps through Functional Digraphs and Fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.08674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We count solutions of composition identities for maps on finite sets, first for three identities in which both maps vary and then for commutation with a prescribed arithmetic map. For $f\circ g=f\circ g\circ g$, drawing an arrow from each element to its image reduces the enumeration to rooted trees attached to directed cycles. For $f\circ f=f\circ g\circ f$, grouping elements with the same $f$-value leads instead to a partition-based enumeration. A classical rooted-forest enumeration leads in both problems to $\mathcal T(x)$, the exponential generating function for rooted labeled trees. For $f=g\circ f\circ g$, the values on the cycles of $g$ determine all remaining values. The exponential generating function $\mathcal D$ for these ordered pairs and the ordinary generating function $\mathcal A$ for endofunctions up to relabeling satisfy $\mathcal D(x)=\mathcal A(\mathcal T(x))$. Finally, we count functions on $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ satisfying $f(ax)=af(x)$, first for prime multipliers $a$ and then for a broader class of composite multipliers. In each problem, fixing one map exposes independent choices for the other through its functional digraph or its fibers.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev

item.title: A counterexample to Manin's Conjecture for almost Fano varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.08890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an example of a smooth rational threefold over a number field with a big anticanonical divisor that does not satisfy the thin set version of Manin's Conjecture. In particular, Manin's Conjecture does not hold for rationally connected almost Fano varieties.
item.dc:creator: Brian Lehmann, Sho Tanimoto

item.title: Zariski dense hyperbolic 3-manifold groups in $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.
item.dc:creator: Dong Hyun Lee

item.title: Cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.09080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension over fields of characteristic zero, extending the definition for curves by Grothendieck. Our notion of cuspidal sections is defined relative to a normal crossings compactification. We prove that the closure of the resulting set is independent of the choice of a compactification. For varieties iteratively constructed from fibrations, we compare our definition to an inductive notion of cuspidal sections, and discuss connections to the section conjecture of Grothendieck.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Carlson, David Corwin

item.title: One complex metric and geometric adelic nefness
item.description: arXiv:2611.09319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that an arithmetic adelic line bundle on a smooth quasi-projective variety over a number field has nef geometric part if its prescribed continuous metric at one complex embedding has semipositive first Chern current. The proof constructs semiample approximations to every positive rational ample perturbation by boundary extension, multiplier ideals, and Nadel vanishing, followed by specialization and Galois descent. This gives geometric nefness of Gao--Zhang's canonical Gross--Schoen adelic line bundle.
item.dc:creator: Kaicheng Dong

item.title: Supercuspidal and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.09555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of cardinality $q$, and let $(K_n)$ be a tower of principal congruence subgroups attached to a lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in the Lie algebra. We show that the proportion of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors carried by supercuspidal representations is $\delta_{\mathrm{ell}}(\Lambda)+O(q^{-n/4})$, where the elliptic density $\delta_{\mathrm{ell}}(\Lambda)>0$ is the probability that a random element of the dual lattice $\Lambda$ is nonzero on the Lie algebra of the unipotent radical of every proper parabolic subgroup. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$ this limit was anticipated by Howe. The error improves to $O(q^{-\tau n/4})$ with an explicit $\tau\in(1,2]$, except when $\mathrm{char}\,F=2$ and $\mathbf{G}$ has an isotropic direct factor which over $\bar F$ is a product of adjoint groups of type $\mathrm{B}_d$. We determine when $\delta_{\mathrm{ell}}(\Lambda)=1$, give an explicit bound uniform in $F$ for reductive models, and deduce a bound uniform over the completions of a global field. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis on congruence quotients, a quantitative Sard theorem for parabolic incidence maps and a Jacquet-module argument; it uses neither a classification of supercuspidal representations nor the exponential map.
item.dc:creator: Erez Lapid, Mark Shusterman

item.title: Qin's Algorithm, Continued Fractions and 2-dimensional Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2310.09103v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In his ``Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections''(1247), Jiushao Qin introduced ``the Dayan method of deriving unity'' for computing modular inverses, an essential component of his treatment of the Chinese remainder theorem. A distinctive feature of Qin's algorithm is its use of a state consisting of four nonnegative integers arranged in a matrix. In this paper, we investigate the mathematical structure of these states and their connections with continued fractions and two-dimensional lattices. By introducing a signed version of the state, we obtain a natural matrix representation that reveals the convergents of continued fractions and gives direct derivations of several classical results. We then show that the signed states form bases of a family of two-dimensional lattices arising from modular congruences. In particular, we prove that a shortest lattice vector can be obtained from the rows of a signed state or their sum or difference. We also study the monotonicity of the inner products of the state vectors and discuss a subsequent result that locates a shortest vector in one of two consecutive states. It is surprising that a shortest lattice vector is found in a highly structure sequence of states. These results demonstrate that the state structure of Qin's algorithm provides a unified framework for understanding modular inversion, continued fractions, and shortest vectors in two-dimensional lattices.
item.dc:creator: Han Wu, Guangwu Xu

item.title: A GL(3) converse theorem via a "beyond endoscopy" approach
item.description: arXiv:2401.04037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a new proof of the converse theorem for Maass forms on ${\rm GL}(3)$ using a technique that is inspired by Langlands' philosophy of "beyond endoscopy", thereby implementing these ideas for the first time in a higher rank setting.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Blomer, Wing Hong Leung

item.title: Triple product $p$-adic $L$-functions for finite slope families and a $p$-adic Gross-Zagier formula
item.description: arXiv:2403.18620v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we generalize two results of H. Darmon and V. Rotger on triple product $p$-adic $L$-functions associated with Hida families to finite slope families. We first prove a $p$-adic Gross-Zagier formula, then demonstrate an application to a special case of the equivariant Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for supersingular elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: Ting-Han Huang

item.title: Values of ternary quadratic forms at integers and the Berry-Tabor conjecture for 3-tori
item.description: arXiv:2601.03209v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Berry and Tabor conjectured in 1977 that spectra of generic integrable quantum systems have the same local statistics as a Poisson point process. We verify their conjecture in the case of the two-point spectral density for a quantum particle in a three-dimensional box, subject to a Diophantine condition on the domain's proportions. A permissible choice of width, height and depth is for example $1,2^{1/3},2^{-1/3}$. This extends previous work of Eskin, Margulis and Mozes (Annals of Math., 2005) in dimension two, where the problem reduces to the quantitative Oppenheim conjecture for quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$. The difficulty in three and higher dimensions is that we need to consider the distribution of indefinite forms in shrinking rather than fixed intervals, which we are able to resolve for special diagonal forms of signature $(3,3)$ in various scalings, including a rate of convergence. A key step of our approach is to represent the relevant counting problem as an average of a theta function on $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})^3\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^3$ over an expanding family of one-parameter unipotent orbits. The asymptotic behaviour of these unipotent averages follows from Ratner's measure classification theorem and subtle escape of mass estimates.
item.dc:creator: Wooyeon Kim, Jens Marklof, Matthew Welsh

item.title: The symmetrized sum of finite $q$-multiple harmonic sums with one exceptional index
item.description: arXiv:2602.02480v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we give explicit expressions for $q$-harmonic sums on $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ indices. The case $A=1$ has been extensively studied, and a variety of identities, explicit evaluations, and structural properties are known. Likewise, numerous explicit evaluations are available for $q$-multiple zeta values and $q$-harmonic sums with uniform indices $A-\cdots-A$. Although several methods are available for treating non-uniform indices, explicit evaluations for the pattern $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ remain comparatively scarce. The case $A=2$ was settled only recently. In this paper, we extend this framework to the general case $A\ge3$ as the total sum with the theory of the elementary symmetric functions, though we do not generally evaluate each summand at a prescribed position of $A$. We obtain explicit formulas in terms of binomial coefficients and degenerate Bernoulli numbers. Some expressions about $2-\cdots-2,A,2-\cdots-2$ are also shown.
item.dc:creator: Hideaki Ishikawa, Takao Komatsu

item.title: Generalized Fermat equation over cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_l$-extensions of totally real fields
item.description: arXiv:2605.20860v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a totally real field of odd degree $m$ in which $2$ is inert. Let $l\geq5$ be a prime totally ramified in $K$ with $\gcd(m,l(l-1)/2)=1$ and $2^{l-1}\not\equiv1\pmod{l^2}$. We prove the asymptotic Fermat's Last Theorem over every layer $K_{n,l}$, $n\geq1$, of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_l$-extension of $K$. Using $S$-unit bounds, we also give criteria for the generalized Fermat equation $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ to have no asymptotic solutions in $K_{n,l}^3$ when the coefficients $A,B,C$ are supported at the primes above $2$ or $2d$, with $d$ an odd prime. In particular, for every fixed integer $r\geq2$ other than $4$, the equation $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no asymptotic solutions in $K_{n,l}^3$ for each fixed $n\geq1$. Thorne's modularity theorem makes the resulting bounds effective in each layer $\mathbb{Q}_{n,l}$ to which our criteria apply.
item.dc:creator: Satyabrat Sahoo

item.title: The Bogomolov property for $p$-supercuspidal eigenforms
item.description: arXiv:2605.31403v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a lower bound on the Weil height, the so-called Bogomolov property, for the algebraic extensions of $\mathbb Q$ cut out by the adelic Galois representations attached to certain eigenforms whose local component at a prime $p$ is supercuspidal. To this end, we give a method for constructing metric inequalities over $p$-adic Lie extensions of fields over $\mathbb Q$ that are finitely ramified at $p$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Conti, Pietro Piras, Lea Terracini

item.title: Divisor moments of polynomials in Fourier coefficients of modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2607.18832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study higher moments of the divisor function evaluated at polynomial expressions in the Fourier coefficients of a non-CM newform. The logarithmic exponent appearing in our estimates depends only on the number of irreducible factors of the polynomial and remains unchanged under a Sato--Tate restriction. The proof combines an effective Chebotarev theorem, or an effective Chebotarev--Sato--Tate theorem, with the arithmetic of joint cycle types and a mean value estimation for multivariable multiplicative functions with Frobenian support.
item.dc:creator: Wonwoong Lee

item.title: Sieve dimension and search depth for the Erd\H{o}s-Straus conjecture, $n \equiv 1 \pmod{24}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.24035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For primes $n\equiv1\pmod{24}$, we study the depth of explicit, factorization-free searches for a decomposition of $4/n$ into three positive unit fractions. Let $E_2(N;J)$ be the set of such primes $n\le N$ for which no coprime pair $1\le u,a\le J$ admits a divisor $s\mid an+u$ with $s\equiv-1\pmod{4ua}$. For every fixed $J$, we prove $|E_2(N;J)|\ll_J N/(\log N)^{1+A(J)/2}$, where $A(J)$ counts the coprime pairs in $[1,J]^2$. The proof uses a fixed-point-free involution and identifies the exact dimension of the covering. We also establish a dual Type I divisor criterion and an unconditional obstruction: at the fixed shift $c=7$, both branches of the cofactor criterion fail for $\asymp N/(\log N)^{3/2}$ primes. At growing depth, an exact reciprocal-totient asymptotic with leading constant $9/(2\pi^2)$ improves the explicit large-sieve bounds to $O(N\exp(-0.0942(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^5$, and to $O_\varepsilon(N\exp(-(0.1093-\varepsilon)(\log N)^{2/3}))$ at cutoff $p>J^{4+\varepsilon}$ for fixed sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Finally, combining a truncated Type I pass with a sparse residual search yields a complete, factorization-free batch decision procedure for all primes in $[N,2N]$, using $O(N^2(\log N)^2\exp(-c_0(\log N)^{2/3}))=o(N^2)$ arithmetic operations for some $c_0>0$. The conjecture itself remains open.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Dahan

item.title: Structure of derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings
item.description: arXiv:2609.34589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings regarded as discrete rings. We compare each such algebra with the degreewise inverse limit of the derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in finite rings and with its subalgebra consisting of elements with uniformly finite double-coset support. Under cohomological comparison hypotheses, the natural map to this subalgebra has image given by its degree-zero part and its positive-degree torsion. We describe the kernel in terms of continuous cohomology and prove that it is a divisible square-zero ideal annihilated by every positive-degree element. These comparisons are compatible with Yoneda products, and the action on torsion Ext classes factors through the image. We compute the resulting algebras for the additive group $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and determine the underlying graded abelian groups for $(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p),\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_p))$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p>3$. The examples exhibit distinct effects of the coefficient topology and the support condition.
item.dc:creator: Shuta Kataoka

item.title: Cubic arithmetic-geometric mean and isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.03100v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct degree-three isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic different from three, which correspond to a step of the cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. As an application, we describe the Serre-Tate canonical lift of an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic three by the 3-adic cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. We also discuss the relations of the Hesse curves with complex and finite hypergeometric functions.

item.title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
item.description: arXiv:2610.24900v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean. By referring to an additional announced uniform zero-free half-plane for general Dedekind zeta functions, we also establish the corresponding result for certain explicit new families of non-Galois cubic, quartic and quintic fields of unit rank one or two.
item.dc:creator: Harald Grobner

item.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.36727v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and linearized polynomials connect field extensions, normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Cyclotomic cosets link additive symmetries and local phase data with polynomial composition, factorization, and compatible lifting. Low-degree subfield representations and relative traces lead to root-block recovery, while return maps on root fibers organize constructions of irreducible polynomials. Coding applications include duality, distance bounds, Fourier support, and syndrome decoding. Character sums yield trace-norm distributions, the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field sums and curve point counts. The final chapter constructs finite fields as residue fields of unramified p-adic extensions and relates Teichmuller representatives and Hensel lifting to cyclotomic orbits, periodic digit expansions, Witt carries, coefficient valuations, and Newton slopes. The emphasis throughout is on explicit proofs and reusable connections between field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.
item.dc:creator: Hongfeng Wu, Li Zhu

item.title: The Quantum Pendulum of Turbulent Flow: Decaying turbulence as a thermal state of an integrable system
item.description:
arXiv:2607.05745v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a theory of decaying turbulence in which the statistics of a classical flow becomes quantum mechanics in loop space. The loop functional, the average of $e^{\mathrm{i}\Gamma/
u}$ for the circulation $\Gamma$ around a loop, is the wave function, and the Navier-Stokes equation becomes the linear loop equation. An exact operator identity represents the functional as the loop-ordered exponential of the covariant derivative $\partial+\mathrm{i}v/
u$, with the loop parameter as time and viscosity as Planck's constant. The turbulent state is the equal-weight density matrix on a decaying trajectory, a quantum form of the ergodic hypothesis. As in quantum field theory, turbulence at infinite Reynolds number is defined by regularization and renormalization; the loop equation regularized on $N$-sided polygons has an exact manifold of decaying solutions, the Euler ensemble, labeled by rational angles and spins. As a fermionic trace, its partition function and conditional vorticity correlations become, in the local limit, Gibbs averages of two Mathieu quantum pendulums, an integrable system. The energy spectrum, given by explicit quadratures, falls as $k^{-1}\log(1/kL)$ at small $k$ and as $k^{-7/2}$ at large $k$, with $L=\sqrt{	ilde
u(t+t_0)}$ and turbulent viscosity $	ilde
u$. At $kL=\sqrt2$ its slope diverges as a double logarithm: the decay at fixed $k$ is singular at a finite time, and the vorticity correlation oscillates with period $\sqrt2\,\pi L$. The reduction to the pendulums, with the continuum and grand canonical limits at every nonzero separation, is formally verified in Lean 4 in forthcoming work by Y. Jiang, A. Migdal et al. The theory rests on stated physical hypotheses, as statistical mechanics rests on the Gibbs distribution; its comparison with simulations and experiment is so far qualitative.

item.title: Modular Existential Closedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.35409v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
